questions.question: Distinguish the roles of shareholders and directors in a company, and explain what fiduciary duty requires of a director. Include what powers shareholders exercise at the annual general meeting and the kinds of directors found on a board.
questions.expected_answer: Shareholders own the company: they provided the capital, their liability is limited to their investment, and they exercise power at the annual general meeting — voting one vote per share, electing and removing directors, appointing the independent auditor and approving the audit fee, receiving and questioning the annual report, and approving major decisions reserved for owners. They receive dividends only when directors declare them. Directors run the company on the shareholders' behalf under a fiduciary duty: act in good faith, in the best interests of the company, never for personal gain, and declare any personal interest in a decision. Their duties include managing operations, safeguarding assets through internal control, preparing financial statements that fairly present, declaring affordable dividends, and accounting to shareholders. The board contains executive directors who work in the company daily, non-executive directors who bring outside oversight, and independent non-executive directors with no other financial ties to the company. Good governance separates the chairperson, ideally an independent non-executive who runs the board, from the chief executive who runs the company.

questions.question: The treasurer of a club — or a director of a company — awards a supply contract to a family member's business without obtaining other quotes. Using the King Code's four demands and the professional ethics principles, diagnose what has gone wrong and recommend the full remedy.
questions.expected_answer: The problem: a decision-maker with an undeclared personal interest steered a contract to a family member without competition. The principles broken: objectivity, because a conflict of interest was allowed to override unbiased judgement; fairness, because other suppliers and the members or shareholders whose money was spent were not fairly treated; and transparency, because the connection was concealed rather than disclosed. Even a competitive price does not repair the breach, because nobody protected the decision. The remedy: declare the family connection as soon as it arises; withdraw entirely from that decision; let the remaining committee members or directors obtain several competing quotes; decide on merit; and record the decision and reasons in the minutes so it can be reviewed. Handled this way the family business may still win the contract honestly. The examination method is three moves: state the problem from the facts, name the principle or duty broken, recommend the remedy that closes it.

questions.question: Describe the three layers through which a company checks itself — internal control, internal audit and the independent audit — including who operates each layer, who each reports to, and why the reporting lines matter. Explain why insider trading and share-price manipulation defeat the purpose of this whole system.
questions.expected_answer: Layer one is internal control, operated daily by management under the directors' responsibility: division of duties so no one person commits and conceals, authorisation of transactions, documentation of every movement, physical safeguards, and regular reconciliation. Layer two is internal audit: employees who test those controls all year and report findings to the audit committee of independent non-executive directors, so a finding cannot be buried by the manager it embarrasses; internal audit recommends, while management stays accountable for acting. Layer three is the independent audit: a registered auditor in public practice, appointed by the shareholders at the annual general meeting, reporting to the shareholders with a published opinion on whether the financial statements fairly present the company's position — an opinion whose entire value rests on the auditor's independence, which the audit committee helps guard. The system exists so outsiders can trust published information. Insider trading uses information the market lacks, and share-price manipulation feeds the market false information — both cheat the very outsiders the reporting and audit chain is built to protect, and both are illegal, carrying dismissal, prosecution and professional expulsion.
